rfi.title: Capital punishment in Pakistan: 'Islam does not promote the death penalty'
rfi.description: Around the world, a total of 47 countries still retain capital punishment – including Pakistan. Barrister Sarah Belal founded the Justice Project Pakistan in 2009 to represent the most vulnerable Pakistani prisoners facing the death penalty, at home and abroad. RFI met her in Paris.

rfi.title: French farmers race to adapt as repeated heatwaves hit crops and livestock
rfi.description: After weeks of sweltering heat and drought, farmers and analysts fear France's maize crop could be down by a third this year – making it the smallest in 35 years. Poultry farmers are also counting their losses as many as 3 million broiler chickens died within a few days in in June. The damage is a result of three heatwaves that have already hit France this year, and is only set to intensify as climate change disrupts agriculture across Europe.

rfi.title: France must speed up climate action, as watchdog warns current efforts fall short
rfi.description: France is not prepared for the pace and scale of climate change, the country’s climate watchdog has warned in a report that calls for a significant acceleration of both emission reduction efforts and adaptation policies, as the country faces its third heatwave since May.

rfi.title: Israel's recognition of the Armenian genocide unsettles Turkey and Azerbaijan
rfi.description: Israel's parliament voted on 29 June 2026 to recognise the 1915 Armenian genocide, breaking with decades of official reticence on the issue. RFI spoke to three regional experts to unpack the politics behind the vote and its fallout: Gerald Steinberg, professor at Bar-Ilan University in Tel Aviv; Richard Giragossian, director of the Regional Studies Centre in Yerevan; and Ilter Turan, professor at Bilgi University in Istanbul.

rfi.description: After almost 1,000 years, the Bayeux Tapestry is back on English soil – spirited to London's British Museum on Friday in the dead of night, after a high-tech and high-security operation in which any slip-up could have spelled disaster.

rfi.title: Mbappé plays down injury fears after France beat Morocco to reach World Cup semis

rfi.title: Secrecy surrounds Bayeux Tapestry's imminent Channel crossing
rfi.description: Under cover of darkness and heavy police guard, the Bayeux Tapestry – a 68-metre embroidered chronicle of the Norman conquest of England, stitched in wool not long after the events it depicts – is set to cross the Channel within days, the official overseeing its move to London has revealed.

rfi.title: How appeal court verdict against Le Pen puts her back in the running for 2027
rfi.description: A French appeals court this week upheld Marine Le Pen's conviction for embezzling funds from the European Parliament and sentenced her to house arrest – something the far-right leader previously said would rule her out of France's 2027 presidential race. Yet Le Pen still has one last legal recourse to overturn her conviction and, pending that appeal, remains free to hit the campaign trail.

rfi.title: Trump says US will give Ukraine licence to build Patriot missiles

lemonde.description: Après le choix par les militants socialistes d’un processus de désignation pour la présidentielle, certaines personnalités ont confirmé leur participation. lemonde.description: Les enfants portent parfois leur casque plusieurs heures d’affilée. Pour préserver leur audition, nous avons comparé des dizaines de casques audio bluetooth ou filaires qui limitent le volume sonore. Nous avons ensuite demandé aux enfants lesquels leur plaisaient le plus. Voici les trois meilleurs.

france24fr.title: Iran : le guide suprême Mojtaba Khamenei a juré de venger la mort de son père
france24fr.description: Le guide suprême iranien Mojtaba Khamenei a juré de venger la mort de son père, Ali Khamenei, tué fin février dans des frappes israélo-américaines, affirmant dans un message écrit diffusé samedi que cette vengeance devait "s'accomplir, inévitablement".

france24fr.title: "Notre terre, notre ciel" : en Cisjordanie occupée, des cerfs-volants face aux colonies
france24fr.description: Un festival de cerfs-volants est organisé chaque année depuis 2009 dans le village de Burin, en Cisjordanie occupée, pour protester contre l'expansion des colonies israéliennes et l'accaparement des terres agricoles dans la région. Entre cerfs-volants aux couleurs du drapeau palestinien, musique et clown pour les enfants, l'événement veut aussi apporter de la légèreté aux habitants.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : des Argentins au mental d'acier avant leur quart de finale face à la Suisse
france24fr.description: Après avoir buté sur les équipes africaines, l'Argentine doit se relancer dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche face à la Suisse en quarts de finale. Avec un billet pour le dernier carré à la clé, les coéquipiers de Lionel Messi ont besoin d'assurer contre les hommes de Murat Yakin, dont la sélection helvétique atteint ce niveau de la compétition pour la première fois depuis 1954.

france24fr.title: France : le projet de loi sur l'usage des armes à feu par les forces de l'ordre divise
france24fr.description: Le texte, adopté mardi dans une Assemblée nationale fracturée, prévoit qu'un policier ou un gendarme soit systématiquement "présumé avoir agi" dans le cadre légal lorsqu'il fait usage de son arme à feu.

france24fr.title: En France, les sans abris, les oubliés de cette canicule
france24fr.description: En France, 24 départements sont placés en vigilance rouge ce samedi en raison de la canicule, la troisième en deux mois. Fin juin, le collectif "Les morts de la rue" indiquait qu'au moins 10 personnes sans-abris étaient décédées lors d'un épisode de chaleur extrême. "Des décès qui auraient pu être évités" explique Lotfi Ouanezar, directeur général d'Emmaüs Solidarité, en rappelant que "les sans abris sont vulnérables et en première ligne face à la chaleur".

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : L'Espagne s'impose sur le fil face à la Belgique et rejoint les Bleus en demies
france24fr.description: L'Espagne s'est imposée à la toute fin du temps réglementaire face aux Diables rouges (2-1), sauvée par un but de Mikel Merino, à la toute fin du temps réglementaire. La Roja a encaissé son premier but sur ce tournoi et affrontera l'Equipe de France mardi 14 juillet en demi-finale de la Coupe du monde.Qui de l'Argentine, la Suisse, l'Angleterre ou la Norvège se qualifiera pour l'autre demie ?Réponse ce samedi soir après Angleterre-Norvège et Argentine-Suisse.

france24fr.title: Troisième vague de chaleur en deux mois en France : 24 départements en vigilance rouge canicule
france24fr.description: En France, 24 départements, dont ceux de la région parisienne, sont placés en vigilance rouge ce samedi en raison de la canicule, la troisième en deux mois, qui attise les incendies dans la moitié sud du pays. “On risque de ne pas pouvoir s’adapter si on continue à réchauffer le climat.” explique Philippe Drobinski, climatologue, directeur de recherche au CNRS et auteur du prochain rapport du GIEC.

france24fr.title: Championnat des nations : le XV de France assomme l'Australie
france24fr.description: Le XV de France a assommé les Wallabies australiens samedi à Brisbane (42-26), avec six essais, dont un doublé de l'ailier Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang pour sa première sélection, lors de la deuxième journée du Championnat des nations entre hémisphère Nord et hémisphère Sud.

france24fr.title: Epidémie d'Ebola : Médecins sans frontières forme des professionnels de santé au Kenya
france24fr.description: Alors que l'épidémie d'Ebola sévit toujours en RD Congo, l'Unicef alerte sur un risque d'aggravation de la situation humanitaire. De son côté, Médecins sans frontières forme des professionnels de santé pour s'entraîner à prendre en charge des patients atteints d'Ebola avant d'être envoyés en RD Congo. Illustration dans un centre de simulation au Kenya.

france24fr.title: Pluies torrentielles, vents violents... Le typhon Bavi s'abat sur Taïwan
france24fr.description: Quelque 900 000 personnes ont été évacuées en Chine à l'approche du typhon Bavi, dont les vents et les pluies ont frappé samedi Taïwan et plusieurs îles japonaises, privant des milliers de foyers d'électricité.

france24fr.title: Une vidéo anti-LFI montrant des musulmans vandaliser une boucherie en Angleterre est générée par IA
france24fr.description: Une vidéo montrant des personnes musulmanes vandaliser une boucherie en Angleterre a été publiée sur X par un compte ouvertement opposé au parti de gauche La France insoumise. Mais elle est générée par intelligence artificielle.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Espagne rejoint la France en demi-finales
france24fr.description: Deux champions du monde se retrouvent en demi-finale de ce Mondial 2026, ce mardi 14 juillet. L'équipe de France, qui a écarté le Maroc (2-0) ce jeudi, et l'Espagne qui a éliminé la Belgique (2-1) vendredi, vont croiser le fer pour s'offrir une place en finale.

france24fr.title: Soudan : les FSR désignées comme organisation terroriste par l'UE
france24fr.description: Le parlement européen a appelé les Etats membres de l'UE à inscrire les Forces de Soutien Rapide sur la liste des organisations terroristes. Depuis trois semaines, El-Obeid, ville assiégée il y a quelques mois par les paramilitaires des Forces de soutien rapide, subit des attaques sans précédent. Pour la première fois, le parlement condamne les soutiens étrangers des FSR en nommant les Émirats Arabes Unis.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : victoire politique pour Diomaye Faye avec l'invalidation de la réforme constitutionnelle
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, le Conseil constitutionnel a invalidé ce jeudi la loi de révision constitutionnelle adoptée le 29 juin par l’Assemblée nationale. Le président, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, avait saisi la plus haute juridiction du pays pour une “violation de la procédure de révision constitutionnelle”. Une nouvelle étape dans le conflit ouvert depuis plusieurs semaines entre l'exécutif et l'Assemblée nationale.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : "les habitants de Kiev se sont réveillés avec le bruit des explosions"
france24fr.description: La capitale ukrainienne Kiev a été frappée samedi par une attaque de missiles russes, qui a fait six blessés, ont affirmé les autorités.

france24fr.title: Feu en Espagne : 12 morts et 6 600 hectares brûlés en Andalousie
france24fr.description: Les autorités attendent les premières autopsies pour pouvoir en dire plus sur le bilan du violent feu de forêt qui a fait au moins 12 morts de nationalités différentes dans la nuit de jeudi à vendredi dans le sud de l'Espagne, dans une zone où vivent de nombreux Britanniques.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Espagne bat la Belgique 2-1
france24fr.description: L'Espagne s'est qualifiée pour les demi-finales de la Coupe du monde 2026 en battant la Belgique (2-1) en quarts vendredi à Los Angeles, et défiera la France mardi pour une place en finale, comme lors du dernier Euro.

france24fr.title: Nouvelle coupure de courant générale à Cuba
france24fr.description: À Cuba, une nouvelle coupure de courant générale a eu lieu. La quatrième en moins de six mois sur fond de blocus pétrolier américain.

zeit.title: Landtagswahl: Die AfD und ihr 100-Tage-Plan für Sachsen-Anhalt
Jürgen Klopp: DFB mit Klopp grundsätzlich über Vertrag einig
zeit.description: Zwischen dem DFB und Jürgen Klopp bahnt sich eine Einigung an. Nach einem Treffen in New York sollen die Eckpunkte für einen Vertrag als Bundestrainer feststehen.

zeit.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Russischer Gleitbombenangriff: Tote und Verletzte in Sumy
Motorrad: Sachsenring-Sprint: Márquez siegt – WM-Zweiter stürzt schwer
Fußball-Nationalmannschaft: DFB vor dem Ziel: Einigung mit Klopp für Bundestrainer-Job
Stefan Evers: Das kann nicht klappen. Oder?
zeit.description: Eine taumelnde CDU tauscht kurz vor der Berlinwahl den Spitzenkandidaten aus – das Hochrisikomanöver könnte sogar aufgehen. Den Hauptgegner sieht Stefan Evers links.

zeit.title: Fußball-Nationalmannschaft: DFB-Führung grundsätzlich einig mit Klopp
Abgeordnetenhauswahl: Evers soll Berliner CDU retten – Wahlkampf unter Zeitdruck
Polizei: Raubserie in Hagen: Haftbefehl gegen 44-Jährigen vollstreckt
GKV-Sparpaket: Tschentscher nennt Kassenreform »Fehlleistung der Bundesregierung«
zeit.description: Hamburgs Bürgermeister kritisiert die Sparpolitik durch die Gesundheitsreform scharf und gibt der Bundesregierung eine Mitschuld. Auch aus den Kommunen gibt es Protest.

zeit.title: VW-Krise: Volkswagen-Betriebsrat sieht Vertrauensverlust bei Belegschaft
zeit.description: Die Stimmung in der Volkswagen-Belegschaft ist schlecht. VW-Chef Oliver Blume macht dem Betriebsrat Vorwürfe wegen fehlender Kommunikation. Es gab erste Proteste.

zeit.title: Sanierungsprogramm der Bahn: Bundesverkehrsminister Schnieder ist unzufrieden mit Bahnsanierungen
zeit.description: Monatelange Komplettsperrungen für Reparaturen und trotzdem wenige Verbesserungen. Patrick Schnieder will das Sanierungskonzept überprüfen und fordert Erklärungen.

zeit.title: Irankrieg: Irans oberster Führer droht mit Rache für den Tod seines Vaters
zeit.description: Nach der Bestattung von Ajatollah Ali Chamenei hat sein Sohn Modschtaba in einer Nachricht Rache geschworen. Zudem meldet der Iran 17 Tote durch US-Angriffe. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Supreme Court :  Die letzte Instanz
zeit.description: Der Supreme Court entscheidet über Abtreibung, Waffen, Wahlen – und immer öfter über sein eigenes Ansehen. Was seine Geschichte über die Politisierung des Rechts erzählt.

observador.title: França detém 32 suspeitos de provocar incêndios
observador.description: As autoridades francesas detiveram 32 suspeitos de provocar incêndios florestais desde o início do verão. Macron recordou que "nove em cada dez incêndios têm origem humana".

observador.title: Philip Roth e um mui respeitável seio
observador.description: Este pequeno livro kafkiano de 1972 está longe do brilhantismo de outras obras rothianas. Mas isso talvez valesse também para a quase totalidade da ficção do último século.

observador.title: Morreu Jayden Adams, jogador da África do Sul no Mundial
observador.description: Adams foi um dos 26 que representou o país no Campeonato do Mundo e considerado um dos "grandes talentos" do futebol nacional. A causa de morte não foi divulgada.

observador.title: Depois do cisma tradicionalista, a rutura progressista?
observador.description: Na Igreja Católica alemã, um projeto reformista progressista está à beira da conclusão. Roma alertou para a possibilidade de uma rutura com a unidade da Igreja — dilacerada pelo cisma tradicionalista.

observador.title: Metrobus chega a Coimbra B e Praça da República até setembro
observador.description: A ligação do 'metrobus' até à Estação Coimbra B, bem como à Praça da República, deverá arrancar entre o final de agosto e o início de setembro, revelou o presidente da Metro Mondego.

observador.title: As notícias das 14h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Portugal terá de fazer grande esforço de adaptação ao calor
observador.description: Nuno Sampaio, diretor executivo da Casa da Arquitetura, propõe eliminar estacionamento para criar zonas com árvores, sombras nos passeios e áreas de descanso ao ar livre.

observador.title: 13h. Exames: "pagamento de horas é patético"
observador.description: Fenprof considera "patético" pagamento de horas a professores por causa dos exames. Sebastião Bugalho recusa contradição com grupo parlamentar sobre imigração.

observador.title: PJ detém mulher suspeita de matar o marido no Seixal
observador.description: Uma mulher de 54 anos foi detida pela Polícia Judiciária "fortemente indiciada" por homicídio qualificado, na forma consumada, que vitimou o seu marido, de 57 anos, no concelho do Seixal.

observador.title: Air Force One. Jornalistas do New York Times intimados
observador.description: Quatro jornalistas terão de testemunhar perante um grande juiz federal em Manhattan esta quarta-feira, após revelarem que o avião oficial da presidência não tinha proteção contra mísseis.

observador.title: Amália alucina em versão chatbot (que não é suposto ser)
observador.description: Lançado há uma semana, uma versão do modelo adaptada a chatbot dá respostas inusitadas. Mas esse não é o objetivo do modelo português, que ainda dá os primeiros passos.

observador.title: Jesus no comando traz a fé que faltava aos portugueses?
observador.description: JJ assume a pasta de Martínez e pede uma seleção que jogue o dobro. Espanha está a beneficiar da sorte? "Haaland mania" quer levar a Noruega às meias, Suíça tenta surpreender Messi e companhia.

observador.title: Uma versão enganadora da história: o mundo depois de 1945
observador.description: "A Maldição de Golias", de Luke Kemp, denuncia as falhas das democracias, revela que o capitalismo está onde menos se espera e olha com saudade para o tempo em que éramos mais felizes — e mais altos.

observador.title: 12h. Governo vai pagar horas extra a professores
observador.description: Sebastião Bugalho enaltece o esforço que está a ser feito pelos docentes. Ainda, Rui Tavares já discursou no primeiro dia de Congresso do Livre.

observador.title: Níveis de alerta sismovulcânicos na Terceira baixam para V1
observador.description: Os níveis de alerta na Terceira foram revistos porque "a atividade sismovulcânica registada desde o início do ano na ilha Terceira tem-se situado a níveis mais baixos".

observador.title: Professores que corrijam exames vão receber horas extra
observador.description: Medida foi anunciada por Sebastião Bugalho na sede do PSD. Em comunicado, o ministério da Educação diz que horas extra serão pagas "pelo trabalho realizado durante o fim de semana".

observador.title: Ex-caçadores são guardiões da floresta e salvam pangolins
observador.description: Um projeto de conservação ambiental ajudou a converter caçadores de pangolins em guardiões da floresta em Angola, permitindo resgatar mais de 50 exemplares deste mamífero ameaçado.

observador.title: Espanha mostra-nos que utilizar os "talismãs" pode funcionar
observador.description: Pelo segundo jogo consecutivo, a Espanha vencer graças a um golo de Mikel Merino na reta final do encontro. Assim, espanhóis e franceses têm encontro marcado nas 'meias'.

nzz.title: Bekannte frühere Brexit-Politikerin Ann Widdecombe getötet – Verdächtiger freigelassen
nzz.description: Die ehemalige Ministerin und Unterhausabgeordnete wurde am Donnerstag in ihrem Haus aufgefunden. Die Umstände ihres Todes sind rätselhaft.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Russland greift Kiew mit ballistischen Raketen an – mindestens zehn Verletzte
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Trump erklärt Waffenruhe mit Iran für  beendet – Gespräche sollen dennoch weitergehen
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar vereinbarten die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe. Doch Trump erklärt diese am Nato-Gipfel für beendet. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Wenn die KI-Blase platzt: Werden wir überhaupt mit den Folgen fertig?
nzz.description: Der Dotcom-Crash war harmlos: Tech-Aktionäre verloren Geld, doch die Wirtschaft drehte sich weiter. Die US-Immobilienkrise ein paar Jahre später trieb das globale Finanzsystem bereits an den Rand des Kollapses. Und wenn nun die KI-Blase platzt? Die Fallhöhe ist gross.

nzz.title: GASTKOMMENTAR - Die unsichtbare Enteignung: wie Staaten ihre Schulden auf Kosten der Sparer loswerden
nzz.description: Es gibt einen Mechanismus, mit dem Staaten ihre Schulden langfristig tilgen können, ohne die Steuern zu erhöhen oder die Ausgaben zu senken. Das Zauberwort sind negative Realzinsen, mit denen sich Staaten langsam und leise entschulden – auf Kosten der Sparer.

nzz.title: Johan Manzambi fehlt der Schweiz auch gegen den Weltmeister Argentinien – der Captain Granit Xhaka strotzt vor dem historischen WM-Viertelfinal trotzdem vor Optimismus
nzz.description: In der Nacht auf Sonntag absolviert das Nationalteam das grösste Fussballspiel der Schweizer Sportgeschichte. Statt nur über Lionel Messi zu reden, fokussieren der Coach und der Captain auf die eigenen Stärken.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK MIT DATEN - Die Legende vom Stillstand der französischen Atomkraftwerke: In der Hitze schwächelten vor allem Windräder
nzz.description: In den heissen Tagen diskutierte Deutschland vor allem über die Reaktoren in Frankreich und der Schweiz. Doch NZZ-Daten zeigen: Das eigentliche Problem trat im eigenen Land zutage.

nzz.title: Die ICE-Beamten verhaften wieder deutlich mehr Ausländer – nun haben sie in Texas einen Mexikaner erschossen
nzz.description: Das Ministerium für Inlandsicherheit sagt, der Tod eines illegal in den USA lebenden mexikanischen Kleinunternehmers sei die Folge einer Verwechslung gewesen. Die mexikanische Regierung kündigt rechtliche Schritte an.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Der Schlagabtausch zwischen Iran und den USA wird anhalten – und Benzin bleibt teuer
nzz.description: Der Erdölmarkt hat den Iran-Krieg besser weggesteckt als gedacht. Aber solange um die Strasse von Hormuz gestritten wird, gibt es keine Entwarnung. Das kann noch lange sein.

nzz.title: Wie sich Europa auf den langen Weg zur eigenen Abschreckung macht
nzz.description: Beim Nato-Gipfel in Ankara stand Donald Trump im Rampenlicht. Doch in seinem Schatten haben Europa und vor allem Deutschland die schärfste strategische Wende seit dem Kalten Krieg eingeleitet.

nzz.title: Braun, süss, klebrig: Kaffeekonzentrat ist das Trendgetränk des Sommers. Mit Kaffee hat es wenig zu tun, aber vielleicht liegt gerade darin das dunkle Geheimnis
nzz.description: In Milch oder Wasser aufgelöst. Mit Eiswürfeln, garniert mit Caramelsirup oder Kokosschaum: Kaffeekonzentrate sorgen in den sozialen Netzwerken für einen Hype.

nzz.title: China und Russland sehen Starlink als Bedrohung – und wollen gemeinsam dagegen vorgehen
nzz.description: Den Medien zugespielte Dokumente zeigen, dass die militärische Kooperation zwischen Peking und Moskau viel weiter geht, als bisher bekannt war.

nzz.title: Nigel Farages ärgster Gegner ist eine Mülltonne – wer ist Count Binface?
nzz.description: Nachdem der Chef von Reform UK eine vorgezogene Wahl in Clacton-on-Sea erzwungen hat, wird sein einziger Rivale voraussichtlich ein Spasskandidat sein, der Farages Kalkül zunichtemacht.

nzz.title: Die ungeheuerliche Tat des besten Freundes: Hal Ebbott hat einen beeindruckenden Debütroman vorgelegt
nzz.description: Der New Yorker Schriftsteller beschreibt in seinem Buch «Unter Freunden», wie das Geburtstagsfest zweier Familien plötzlich alles infrage stellt, was während Jahrzehnten aufgebaut worden ist.

nzz.title: Wütende Ärzte und zerstrittene Physiotherapeuten: Die mächtige Lobbymaschine des Gesundheitswesens stottert
nzz.description: Verbände gestalten die Gesundheitspolitik massgeblich mit. Doch mit internen Kämpfen wie jenem bei der FMH und bei Physioswiss schwächen sie sich selbst. Der Bund steuert dafür umso mehr.

nzz.title: Ein Opfer der Bundesbeteiligung? Warum die Swisscom in die zweite Börsenliga absteigt
nzz.description: Die Aktien der Ex-Monopolistin werden im Herbst den Börsen-Leitindex  SMI verlassen. Die Swisscom kämpft weiter gegen den Bedeutungsverlust und sucht Wachstum im Ausland.

spiegel.title: Supermarkt: Warum ich beim Einkaufen an mir selbst scheitere
spiegel.description: Warmer Atem, kaltes Licht und rempelnde Menschen: Nirgendwo scheitere ich so sehr an mir wie in einem Supermarkt.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: DFB und Klopp über »Eckpunkte eines potenziellen Vertrages« einig
spiegel.description: Die Verhandlungen zwischen dem DFB und dem Wunsch-Bundestrainer Jürgen Klopp schreiten voran. Argentiniens Fußballverband ist offenbar Opfer einer Cyberattacke geworden. Und: Für Lothar Matthäus kommt Lionel Messi nicht als Weltfußballer infrage. Die WM-News.

spiegel.title: Gebäudemodernisierungsgesetz: Grüne melden verfassungsrechtliche Bedenken an
spiegel.description: Der Bundestag hat am Freitag das Heizungsgesetz der Ampelregierung gekippt – zum Unmut der Opposition. Nun bitten die Grünen das Bundespräsidialamt um Beistand.

spiegel.title: Iran: Neuer Oberster Führer Mojtaba Khamenei kündigt Rache an
spiegel.description: Seit Monaten ist Irans neuer Oberster Führer Mojtaba Khamenei nicht öffentlich in Erscheinung getreten. Nach neuen Drohungen Donald Trumps hat er sich nun geäußert, allerdings nur schriftlich.

spiegel.title: Irak: Bundeswehrabzug aus Erbil – scharfe Kritik an Boris Pistorius
spiegel.description: Die Bundeswehr wird ihr Feldlager in Erbil aufgeben. Aus dem Bundestag kommt heftige Kritik an der Entscheidung von Verteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius – vor allem aus den Fraktionen der Koalition.

spiegel.title: NBA: Bam Adebayo schlägt nach Instagram-Streit auf Ex-Teamkollegen Tyler Herro ein
spiegel.description: Bam Adebayo schaffte in dieser Saison 83 Punkte in einem Spiel. Tyler Herro spielte lange an seiner Seite, musste Miami Heat aber kürzlich verlassen. Danach gab es Ärger in den sozialen Medien, nun ist der Konflikt eskaliert.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM: Was Erling Haalands Traumtor mit Lionel Messi verbindet
spiegel.description: Gegen Brasilien hat Erling Haaland eines der faszinierendsten Tore der WM geschossen. Warum der Treffer an Lionel Messi erinnert – und typisch für Haaland ist.

spiegel.title: AfD und Medien: Dunja Hayali, Alice Weidel und die Fallstricke des engagierten Journalismus
spiegel.description: Keine Partei wird von den etablierten Medien so kritisch betrachtet wie die AfD. Warum wird sie dann immer erfolgreicher?

spiegel.title: Österreich: Wem gehören die Habsburger-Juwelen – Podcast
spiegel.description: Mehr als 100 Jahre galten der legendäre »Florentiner«-Diamant und weitere Kronjuwelen der Habsburger als verschollen. Nun sind sie wieder da – und mit ihnen der Streit, wem sie gehören.

spiegel.title: Ammerbuch: 70-Jähriger überrollt Ehefrau mit Mähdrescher
spiegel.description: Sie habe ihm etwas zu trinken reichen wollen, er habe beim Rauslehnen unbeabsichtigt den Mähdrescher gestartet: Bei einem Unfall auf einem Feld ist eine Frau am Bein schwer verletzt und anschließend ins Krankenhaus gebracht worden.

spiegel.title: Düsseldorf-Köln: Verdacht auf Sabotage nach Böschungsbrand
spiegel.description: Wurde an der Bahnstrecke zwischen Düsseldorf und Köln absichtlich Feuer gelegt? Ein Bekennerbrief wird von Ermittlern als authentisch eingeschätzt. Unklar ist, wann der gesperrte Abschnitt wieder freigegeben wird.

spiegel.title: VW: Betriebsrat will Vorstandschef Oliver Blume vor die Belegschaft zitieren
spiegel.description: Der Volkswagen-Konzern ringt um seine Zukunft – und verhandelt ein Sparpaket. Doch der Graben zwischen Geschäftsführung und Mitarbeitern wird tiefer. Die Beschäftigten verlangen Informationen.

spiegel.title: Taiwan und China: Tausende bringen sich vor Taifun in Sicherheit
spiegel.description: Die Wetterbehörde warnt vor gefährlichen Riesenwellen und extremem Starkregen: In Taiwan blieben Geschäfte geschlossen, Tausende Haushalte waren ohne Strom. Am Sonntag soll der Sturm in China auf Land treffen.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Kyjiw beschießt russische Öltanker
spiegel.description: In der Nacht hat die Ukraine 21 russische Schiffe mit Drohnen angegriffen. In Kyjiw herrschte Luftalarm, mehrere Menschen wurden durch russische Raketen verletzt.

Faced with observations of early black holes and galaxies that weren’t expected to exist, scientists have come up with a wealth of new theories to explain them. Now they just need to figure out which ones are true.

new-sci.title: This book is essential reading before watching the new Odyssey film

new-sci.description: An experiment with a charged molecule of bismuth and carbon reveals how effects from Albert Einstein’s special relativity reshape the standard understanding of chemical bonds

new-sci.title: Injection halves risk of chromosome error common in older human eggs
new-sci.description: Egg cells missing a key protein may be more likely to end up with the wrong number of chromosomes, but an mRNA injection that helps the cells make the protein reduces the problem

new-sci.title: A worm that lived half a billion years ago preferred turning right
new-sci.description: Fossils of Spriggina floundersi provide the earliest evidence of animals favouring one side of the body over the other – a feature of nervous systems that we see in our own right- and left-handedness

new-sci.description: Feedback is delighted by a study of how many animals produce poop that echoes the look of the poop emoji – even the lugworm, which does it upside down

new-sci.title: The 4 best science-fiction shows of 2026 so far
new-sci.description: The first six months of 2026 have seen bright threads in sci- fi series including Fallout and Paradise. But for pure gold, advises TV columnist Bethan Ackerley, try Star City

new-sci.title: Seeding clouds with seawater could prevent a super El Niño
new-sci.description: A modelling study suggests marine cloud brightening could shade the eastern Pacific and reduce a global temperature spike from El Niño, but there could be unexpected consequences

new-sci.title: Our fertility window could be extended by making ovaries softer
new-sci.description: A drug that softens the ovaries helped mice and rats conceive more easily at an older age, and produce more pups

new-sci.title: Occam’s razor has lost its edge. Can we sharpen our search for truth?
new-sci.description: Seeking out the simplest, most elegant explanations has served scientists well for centuries, but cognitive scientist Marina Dubova’s experiments are revealing better ways to uncover reality

phys-org.title: The 'safe third country' concept turns out to be an empty shell
phys-org.description: In her recently completed research, Dr. Gaia Romeo exposes the reality behind the EU's 'safe third country' policy. She focuses on the only case in which that policy has already been applied on a large scale: Greece. There, the concept was used to reject asylum applications and return asylum seekers under the return policy resulting from the 2016 EU-Turkey Statement.

phys-org.title: Saturday Citations: Blue zone longevity; soft tissue find predates dinosaurs; black hole collisions simplified
phys-org.description: This week, researchers reported finding nanoplastics in Antarctic soils for the first time, suggesting they were delivered via long-range atmospheric transport. A study associates the use of hormonal birth control with the risk of brain tumors. And researchers developed a new drug against metastatic prostate cancer using human proteins.

phys-org.title: Grasses provide most of the world's calories—but we're only now starting to learn how they grow
phys-org.description: If we want to dismiss something as irrelevant, we'd say that it's "as boring as watching the grass grow." And yet grasses—including corn, wheat and rice—make up most of the plant-based calories humans eat, as well as most of the calories fed to livestock. phys-org.title: Intricate molecular mechanisms help bacteria evade immune detection
phys-org.description: Northwestern Medicine scientists have identified a novel mechanism used by the bacteria responsible for gonorrhea to evade immune detection and achieve widespread infection, according to a recent study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes gonorrhea, which is one of the most common sexually transmitted infections. If not treated promptly with antibiotics, the disease can cause infertility, sepsis and pregnancy complications.

phys-org.title: Drought threatens irrigation in northern Italy
phys-org.description: Water reserves are being depleted rapidly in northern Italy, threatening farming as the region's main river dries up, local officials warned Friday.

phys-org.title: Brutal heat wave forecast for western US this weekend
phys-org.description: A "widespread and significant" heat wave is predicted to bring oppressive temperatures to drought-hit western U.S. states over the weekend, with all-time records at risk of falling, the National Weather Service said Friday.

phys-org.title: Thousands shelter in Taiwan as typhoon lashes Japan islands
phys-org.description: More than 14,000 people in Taiwan have fled their homes, and many shops remain closed, as a typhoon pounding Japan's remote southwestern islands swept toward China on Saturday.

phys-org.title: Japan's space agency conducts first test flight for experimental reusable rocket
phys-org.description: Japan's experimental reusable rocket took off and safely landed in a first test flight Saturday as the country seeks to achieve the technology key to cut launch costs and compete in the global space market dominated by SpaceX.

phys-org.title: New platform creates digital map for marine biobanks
phys-org.description: A new digital platform developed under the leadership of CIIMAR is making Portugal's marine biodiversity more accessible by bringing together thousands of biological resources into a single access point. The Blue Biobanks Digital Research Platform aims to bridge scientific research and industry by simplifying the identification of organisms and biological materials with potential applications in areas such as biotechnology, bioremediation, aquaculture, health, cosmetics and many others.

phys-org.title: Collective agreements are least common where workers need them most
phys-org.description: Workers earning the lowest wages are the least likely to be covered by collective agreements in Germany, despite being the group for whom these protections are arguably most important. In 2021, only 34% of workers in the lowest wage decile were covered by collective agreements, compared with more than 60% of workers in the middle of the wage distribution, according to findings of a new report by the ROCKWOOL Foundation Berlin (RFBerlin) and the Institute for Employment Research (IAB) in Nurember

phys-org.title: Understanding anti-blackness at Hispanic-serving research universities
phys-org.description: At Hispanic-Serving Institutions (HSIs), conversations about diversity often center on supporting Hispanic/Latine students. New research from scholars at University of New Mexico highlights an important and sometimes overlooked issue--the experiences of Black students at these universities, specifically those classified as R1, or highly research-intensive institutions.

phys-org.title: Geoscientists reveal how Earth's forces are shaping the 'Roof of the World'
phys-org.description: Geoscientists at the University of Glasgow have helped reveal new evidence about the formation of one of the highest mountainous areas on Earth—the Tibetan Plateau. A study by an international team of Chinese and U.K. geoscientists shows that the unique topography at the summit of the plateau is shaped by processes going on deep in Earth.

phys-org.title: To ancient astronomers, Theta Eridani was brighter for 1,000 years—now we know why
phys-org.description: There's a bit of a historical mystery surrounding the star Theta Eridani. Ptolemy in the second century A.D. and al-Sufi in A.D. 964 both recorded Theta Eridani as one of the 13 brightest stars in the sky. Hipparchus may have said the same. But there's a problem. For it to be one of the 13 brightest, it had to be much more luminous than it is today.

phys-org.title: New sensors capture warning signs before fish deaths in Lake Victoria
phys-org.description: Researchers from King's College London recorded the warning signs of a major low-oxygen event in Lake Victoria just hours before fish deaths were reported by local communities, demonstrating why earlier warning systems are urgently needed.

phys-org.title: Dark energy flips its sign, but the Hubble tension refuses to budge
phys-org.description: For nearly a century, astronomers have known that the universe is expanding. In the late 1990s, two independent teams, the Supernova Cosmology Project, led by Saul Perlmutter, and the High-Z Supernova Search Team, led by Brian Schmidt and Adam Riess, discovered something strange: The expansion is speeding up. phys-org.title: Children back group claims over evidence, but privacy reduces bias, experiments reveal
phys-org.description: As we move closer to Election Day 2026, voting preferences are moving back into focus—and with them, analyses of what drives partisanship at the polls. However, less frequently asked is when Americans show evidence of partisan behavior: shortly or well after reaching the legal voting age? As teenagers? In elementary school?

phys-org.title: Why natural forests survive heat waves better than planted forests
phys-org.description: When a record-breaking drought and heat wave swept across China's Yangtze River Basin in 2022, forests across the region faced an extreme test. The event provided a rare opportunity for researchers to test how different forests respond when rising temperatures and water shortages strike at the same time.

phys-org.title: Moderate warming rewires one-third of microalga's genes, study finds
phys-org.description: Researchers have demonstrated for the first time that the microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii alters the activity of about one-third of its protein-coding genes in response even to moderate temperature changes. The study, published in the journal The Plant Cell, points to far-reaching consequences of climate change for aquatic ecosystems and soil. The research team is from the Cluster of Excellence Balance of the Microverse at Friedrich Schiller University Jena and the Leibniz Institute for Natu

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: The Israel-Lebanon Recipe for Never-Ending War
proj-syn.description: Lebanon’s political circumstances, together with Iran’s strengthened regional position, make Hezbollah’s complete disarmament highly unlikely. By conditioning Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanon on this outcome—but with no provisions about cutting Hezbollah’s Iranian lifeline—the new framework agreement is dead on arrival.

proj-syn.title: Why This Energy Shock Is Different
proj-syn.description: Unlike recent energy crises, today’s geopolitical shock is destroying supply rather than rerouting it, exposing the limits of the standard policy toolkit. Governments can mitigate its impact on those most exposed, but only if fiscal and monetary policy work in concert.

proj-syn.title: China’s Erasure of Tibet Is Accelerating
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the international community has stood idly by while China has systematically eradicated Tibetan culture and identity. With the authorities stepping up their assimilation efforts, Asia risks not only losing one of its oldest civilizations, but also facing a China that is bigger, bolder, and more powerful than ever.

proj-syn.title: Judging the Enhanced Games
proj-syn.description: If fairness in sports required a level playing field that all who wish to compete could afford, that would be a reason for banning expensive performance-enhancing drugs. But it would be a reason for banning expensive high-tech swimming suits and expensive high-tech running shoes, too.

proj-syn.title: What Is the Digital-Money Debate Really About?
proj-syn.description: Both the US and Europe are moving to create digital money, but neither has the right idea about how to do it. The key is to allow “narrow banks,” which issue money but not credit, to keep their reserves in central banks and provide capped interest payments to coin holders.

proj-syn.title: An Athenian View of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: At 250, America is now producing a mindless, raw power and exponentially growing instability. The possibility of catharsis that characterized the United States at its bicentennial is hard to envisage a half-century later—to the detriment of us all.

proj-syn.title: Low-Cost Solutions to Maternal Mortality Already Exist
proj-syn.description: As foreign aid declines, policymakers in lower-income countries must increasingly focus on making better use of scarce resources. When it comes to maternal mortality, that means investing in simple, proven, and affordable interventions for postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia, and obstructed labor.

proj-syn.title: Postmodern Economics
proj-syn.description: Eschewing the idea of a single truth, the recently deceased English artist David Hockney showed that the world unfolds before us in ways we cannot fully understand. After long clinging to the pretense of certainty, economists would do well to embrace the same insight.

proj-syn.title: Digital Public Infrastructure Is Now a Strategic Battleground
proj-syn.description: Digital identity platforms, payment systems, and data exchanges promise more efficient, inclusive, and responsive public services. But in an era of geopolitical rivalry and concentrated digital power, those same systems create strategic dependencies that governments can no longer afford to ignore.

proj-syn.title: Should the Bank of Japan Raise Interest Rates?
proj-syn.description: At the beginning of 2013, when "Abenomics" was rolled out in Japan, the yen was significantly overvalued, and looser monetary policy was badly needed. Today, the opposite is true, indicating that interest-rate hikes may well be the right prescription for Japan.

proj-syn.title: How Argentina Can Protect Its Resource Wealth
proj-syn.description: Alaska, Norway, and Chile recognized the economic and political risks that accompany commodity booms and established sovereign wealth funds to preserve their resource revenues. Argentina’s hydrocarbon- and lithium-rich provinces should learn from their experience.

proj-syn.title: Reinventing Development Finance
proj-syn.description: Faced with shrinking concessional finance and rising borrowing costs, Rwanda has worked with the World Bank Group to leverage limited public funds and risk-sharing instruments to unlock private capital at scale and on affordable terms. It's an arrangement holding important lessons for low-income countries that must do more with less.

proj-syn.title: Mamdani’s American Dream
proj-syn.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Independence Day address was a perfect example of ideology in the positive sense of the term. It overturned both the right-wing populist narrative of the United States and the left-wing "woke" critique with a vision that has the potential to mobilize a majority.

proj-syn.title: How Vulnerable Are US Financial Markets?
proj-syn.description: Fueled by more than $1 trillion in borrowed money and rising leverage across the financial system, US stock markets may have entered bubble territory. Two developments could trigger a sharp correction: higher interest rates and a loss of confidence in the handful of tech giants driving the AI boom.

proj-syn.title: Concessional Finance Is Needed More Than Ever
proj-syn.description: As debt burdens rise and climate shocks intensify, sustainable financing mechanisms are becoming indispensable. The Islamic Development Bank’s new concessional fund offers a promising model for mobilizing the resources needed to protect development gains and invest in resilience.

proj-syn.title: Ruling Class Clowns
proj-syn.description: By the end of the 19th-century in the US, it was clear to all interested observers that market power did not automatically or even easily translate into political capital and cultural authority. That is why, unlike the oligarchs of our time, certain Gilded Age capitalists learned how to become a ruling class.

proj-syn.title: The Missing Ingredient for European Tech Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: Europe’s dependence on US technology companies is both an economic challenge and a strategic vulnerability. The European Union’s new Tech Sovereignty Package is a step in the right direction, but without equally ambitious efforts to curb market concentration, it is bound to fall short.

proj-syn.title: In Praise of the World Cup’s Little Guys
proj-syn.description: In a world of great-power rivalry and hyper-scaling tech behemoths, you would be forgiven for thinking that the bulky bully always has the edge. But as this year's World Cup has shown repeatedly, you would be wrong.
